name: caddy
description: `caddy upgrade`/add-package downloads a fresh binary and overwrites+execs the running exe with no hash/signature.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Caddy exposes explicit commands for updating its executable and package composition through its build service. The reviewed source supports this channel identification; an overall publisher-authentication or vulnerability classification is not established by this review.
limitations: Newly retrieved default-branch snapshot, not historical release re-verification; caddyserver.com service behavior, artifact signing, and any controls outside this command path were not audited.

original_evidence.text: | caddy | github.com/caddyserver/caddy | Go | Y | manual (user runs `caddy upgrade`/`add-package`/`remove-package`; EXPERIMENTAL) | Y | https, default Go TLS validation (no InsecureSkipVerify on this path; repo-wide InsecureSkipVerify hits are all in unrelated reverse-proxy/TLS-pool modules, not the upgrade code) | N (no manifest at all) | none — binary is written straight to disk with no hash or signature check | n/a (none used) | `cmd/packagesfuncs.go` — `cmdUpgrade`/`cmdAddPackage`/`cmdRemovePackage` all call `upgradeBuild()`, which does `http.Get(downloadPath+"?"+qs)` (`downloadPath = "https://caddyserver.com/api/download"`, line ~330) then `writeCaddyBinary()` (io.Copy straight from response body to the executable path, no checksum/signature check anywhere in the file) then immediately `exec.Command(path, "list-modules", ...)` / `exec.Command(path, "version")` to run the freshly-downloaded binary. Registered in `cmd/commands.go:407-417` as "Upgrade Caddy (EXPERIMENTAL)". Confirmed via grep: no `sha256`/`checksum`/`signature` string anywhere in `cmd/*.go`. |
